feed.title: Underkeel notes
feed.subtitle: Measurements of exit cost and liquidations in Morpho Blue markets on Base

entry.title: $91.7M liquidated on Morpho on Base as BTC fell 10.8%
entry.summary: cbBTC carried nine-tenths of it, and Base's pools for it stayed deep. In two markets where the site shows a sale breaking, the collateral seized added up to more than that sale, but in pieces.
entry.content: Liquidations on Morpho Blue on Base repaid $91.7M of debt on Friday and Saturday, 20 and 21 November, two-fifths of all they repaid in the month to 22 November. Bad debt written off against lenders came to less than a cent. I leave out five unlisted markets created during the fall, which look like tests.

entry.title: USDe/USDC debt fell $94.7M in ten hours; its $1M exit held at 38%
entry.summary: From 14 to 20 November, USDe/USDC borrowers took 90.3M USDe out with their repayments and sold none of it in those transactions, SOL/USDC 62.5% gained pool depth, and cbLTC/USDC 62.5% lost a maker.
entry.content: From 15:00 UTC on 19 November, borrowers in USDe/USDC 91.5% repaid $94.7M of their $329.0M debt in under ten hours. The cost of selling $1M of USDe did not move: about 38% in the snapshots before the first repayment and after the last, against a break-even of 2.55%, the cost at which a liquidation pays nothing.

entry.title: Borrowers made 60% of the debt in reach safe before the November low
entry.summary: Between 12 and 15 November, the Morpho markets on Base lending USDC at the lowest LLTV, 62.5%, had 9.0% of their debt liquidated. Those at 86% had 5.2%.
entry.content: In the four days from 12 to 15 November, the nine Morpho markets on Base that carried nearly all the liquidations had $241.9M of debt in reach of the fall. Liquidations took 40% of it.

entry.title: A 12.68% bonus breaks even at an 11.25% exit cost
entry.summary: Until 16 November this site set the cost of selling seized collateral against the liquidation bonus. A liquidator breaks even at a lower cost: 11.25% when the bonus is 12.68%. This note is the correction.
entry.content: At 06:23 UTC on 17 November a $1M sale of cbXRP into USDC on Base cost 12.03%. The cbXRP/USDC 62.5% market on Morpho pays a 12.68% bonus, and until 16 November I would have shown that sale here with 0.65 points of room. The liquidation behind it loses money.

entry.title: A $1M USDe sale on Base costs 37.7% against a 2.55% break-even
entry.summary: USDe/USDC 91.5% is the second largest Morpho market on Base, with $329M borrowed. On 17 November a $200k sale of USDe cost 0.10%, and a $1M sale cost 37.7%.
entry.content: Selling $200k of USDe into USDC on Base cost 0.10% at 06:23 UTC on 17 November. Selling $1M cost 37.7%. A liquidation in the USDe/USDC 91.5% market on Morpho pays only while the sale costs less than 2.55%.

entry.title: Two minutes when a 12.7% bonus was not enough in cbXRP/USDC on Base
entry.summary: On 8 November the cbXRP pools on Base gave way under sales of seized collateral, and positions in Morpho's cbXRP/USDC 62.5% market stood liquidatable for up to 80 seconds. No bad debt followed.
entry.content: At 21:53 UTC on 8 November cbXRP traded 0.2% below Coinbase in the pools on Base, and three minutes later 9.1% below. In the ten seconds when the pools fell fastest, 89% of the cbXRP sold into them came from transactions that also liquidated a position in Morpho's cbXRP/USDC 62.5% market. The liquidations made their own exit expensive: in all three blocks I read over the next minute, selling even $5k of cbXRP cost more than the bonus covers.
